reason_not_testable: Design and ownership proposal only; no executable product change. Validate source trace, JSON, decision matrix and proposed task DAG instead of inventing a RED/GREEN implementation result.
recommendation: Versioned authenticated encryption of destination passwords using the already-required mbedTLS library and a dedicated operator-provisioned keyring file outside database/config backup volumes. Preserve existing API secret omission/clear/revision semantics. Do not reuse the LPR key or its environment-value contract.

protects: Read-only disclosure of new-format destination database rows or database backups when the separate keyring is unavailable to the reader.
Detection of modified ciphertext/tag/nonce or substitution between destination UUIDs through authenticated data.
does_not_protect: Root, the NVR runtime account, a compromised NVR process or a party holding both keyring and database.
Whole-database replay/rollback, hostile filesystem writers, lost hardware, core/swap exposure or an unqualified entropy source.
Historical plaintext copies, old backups, WAL/journal remnants, operator exports, or other credential classes such as stream URLs/LPR.
deployment_preconditions: One writable NVR instance/database per dedicated destination key; never share a write key across cloned installations.
Trusted operator controls provisioned keyring and restore workflow. Restored/cloned databases receive a fresh active write key before credential writes.
No claim of FIPS certification, hardware-backed custody or physical target qualification.

provider.selector: LIGHTNVR_EVENT_KEYRING_FILE contains an absolute path only, never key material

file_contract.keys: One active and optionally one old decrypt-only slot; each holds a unique ID and exactly 32 externally generated random bytes encoded as 64 hexadecimal characters. No key values are included in this proposal.

validation: Bounded read through an O_CLOEXEC, O_NOFOLLOW descriptor; regular file; owner equals runtime UID; no group/other permissions; reject unsafe writable parent directories.
Strict JSON/version/field/length checks; duplicate IDs and identical active/old key material rejected. Never log parser input or key bytes.
File is outside configured database, recording, config export and application backup roots; compare canonical paths and reject aliases into those roots.
Capture one immutable startup snapshot, validate descriptor identity/size around read, close descriptor and zero temporary buffers. No shell expansion or remote URL provider.
Symlink-projected Kubernetes secrets are not automatically supported by this strict initial provider; require separately designed trusted-anchor resolution before enabling that deployment.
provider.lifetime: Keyring snapshot lives only in the NVR process until orderly shutdown, with explicit zeroing. File replacements/removal take effect only on restart; this is not hot key revocation. No environment key values passed to managed children.
provider.provisioning: External operator/secret-manager procedure generates and escrows a fresh dedicated 256-bit key, installs file with runtime UID ownership and 0400 or 0600 permissions, mounts read-only, then starts service. Application never generates a replacement key when an existing key is missing.

envelope.library: mbedtls_gcm_crypt_and_tag in ENCRYPT mode; mbedtls_gcm_auth_decrypt for authenticated decrypt
envelope.plaintext_bytes: Existing MQTT password bytes, 1..255, excluding terminal NUL; empty credential is represented as no envelope.
envelope.aad: Length-prefixed byte fields (unsigned 32-bit big-endian lengths): ASCII lightnvr:event-destination:password:v1, canonical 36-byte destination UUID, key ID. Mutable profile revision/name/host are excluded so noncredential updates do not require decryption.
envelope.nonce_policy: Fresh 96-bit OS-entropy nonce for each encryption attempt. Reject entropy errors and a collision with any currently stored nonce for that key; no timestamps, PRNG seed fallback or intentional nonce reuse. This bounded current-row check cannot detect all historical collisions: the random construction and lifetime invocation limit provide the probabilistic bound, not a claim of deterministic global uniqueness.
envelope.invocation_accounting: A durable credential_key_usage table reserves and commits an encryption-attempt count before cryptography, including failed/stale/rolled-back attempts. Cap at 2^32 attempts per key across this single writer; exhaustion requires fresh key rotation. Never reclaim counts. Restore/clone requires fresh active write key because accounting in a restored database can roll back.
envelope.limits: Current small bounded password/AAD lengths only. Entropy/provider compatibility and accounting under crash/retry must be tested; this proposal is not a cryptographic certification.
envelope.failure: Reject malformed lengths/version/key ID, unavailable key, nonce/accounting failure or bad authentication tag. Zero entire output buffer; never return partial plaintext or interpret ciphertext/legacy bytes as a password.
envelope.key_separation: Do not share LIGHTNVR_LPR_MASTER_KEY_HEX material or derive keys ad hoc. Dedicated operator provisioned destination key only.

schema_proposal.version: 0091 is a proposed next slot, not reserved or applied; coordinator must check current migration head before materialization.
columns: Rename password to legacy_password so an old binary cannot silently read an empty password or write a new plaintext password through its old SQL.
Add credential_version, credential_key_id, credential_nonce BLOB, credential_ciphertext BLOB and credential_tag BLOB with shape CHECK constraints.

Version 0 with empty legacy_password and NULL envelope means no password. Version 0 with nonempty legacy_password means migration pending and is never read for delivery. Version 1 requires empty legacy_password and a complete valid-shape envelope.
guards: Reject new/changed nonempty legacy_password values after structural upgrade; only preservation of existing pending values or clearing them is permitted.
Preserve destination UUID, enabled state, revision concurrency, names, username, TLS settings, routes and outbox references.
Add credential_key_usage keyed by key ID with nonnegative bounded encryption-attempt count; counter reservations are separate committed work from later credential row transactions.
schema_proposal.legacy_binary: Old destination SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE password-column operations fail explicitly after rename. This is feature-level fail-closed behavior, not a promise that an old entire binary refuses startup. Direct old-binary use is unsupported.
schema_proposal.downgrade: Down migration explicitly aborts; never export plaintext or drop envelope guards to make downgrade appear to work. Restore only through the qualified new-binary recovery workflow.

operation_semantics.result: Validate provider/accounting, allocate UUID, encrypt before SQLite binding, then atomically insert only envelope and metadata. Key/entropy failure yields explicit credentials_unavailable (proposed HTTP 503) with no destination/audit success mutation.
Preserve current envelope/key ID or pending legacy value byte-for-byte; update allowed metadata with expected revision. No decryption required. Do not silently change password_configured.

Encrypt under active key first, then compare expected revision and atomically replace envelope. Stale/failed write leaves old credential and revision intact; reserved crypto invocation remains consumed.

Authorized expected-revision update clears logical legacy/envelope fields, marks unconfigured, and restarts affected runtime client through existing generation/revision behavior. This is deliberate clear, not a fallback on decryption failure; no physical-erasure claim.

Continue returning metadata and password_configured only. Do not return plaintext, envelope, nonce/tag or provider contents. A configured-but-locked destination remains configured; expose only nonsensitive existing failure/health state.

Require expected revision, active ready state and verified envelope authentication. Plaintext exists in the scoped buffer and mosquitto client copy only as required for authentication; zero caller buffer and destroy old client on revision change.

NVR recording and metadata management may start; credential-dependent destinations stay blocked with observable configuration failure. Preserve pending outbox entries under existing retry/retention policy, never acknowledge delivery or fall back to anonymous/legacy plaintext. Empty-password destinations retain their existing explicit semantics.

Immutable already-loaded snapshot remains valid until controlled shutdown; revocation requires stop/restart and, for broker credentials, broker-side revocation. Do not promise instant filesystem-triggered revocation.

operation_semantics.operation: unknown live key ID or active-key change
operation_semantics.result: Block affected credentials and writes; require offline rotation/recovery before resuming. Do not create mixed-key live writes merely because a new keyring was mounted.

Recommended: reject automatic/new manual DB backup/export with explicit credential_migration_pending rather than creating more plaintext copies; retain existing backups unchanged. Availability/recovery tradeoff requires D1 approval.

migration.structural: Apply additive envelope schema/legacy-column rename transactionally through existing migration tooling; generated embedded header and T29 current-schema assertion must change together. Historical 0.45.0 fixture bytes remain unchanged.
migration.data: Before destination workers/delivery start, bound scan to EVENT_DESTINATION_MAX_COUNT=64. With validated key snapshot, reserve attempts, encrypt pending secrets in memory and atomically commit all affected credential rows plus migration-ready marker. Any row/crypto/auth/write error rolls back data conversion; pending values remain blocked, not read for runtime delivery.
migration.crash: Crash before data commit leaves pending legacy rows; restart retries only with valid provider and fresh nonces/consumed accounting. Crash after commit reads complete envelopes. No half-written credential state or auto-plaintext recovery.
migration.preservation: Only credential representation changes; preserve revisions for pure representation migration and verify UUID/routes/outbox associations. Online password writes retain their existing revision bumps.
migration.history: Logical conversion is not forensic erasure. Existing DB free pages, WAL/journal, snapshots and backups can still hold old secrets. Protected maintenance/checkpoint/rewrite and actual raw artifact scans are separate closure checks; do not delete live WAL files or claim SSD/cloud snapshot erasure.
migration.broker_rotation: After legacy exposure inventory/retirement, operator must consider rotating broker-side passwords; encryption of a new DB cannot revoke a password leaked in an old copy. No remote broker mutation is authorized by this proposal.

rotation_restore.broker_password_rotation: Existing authenticated API replace remains online: new plaintext is encrypted under current master key, revision increments, worker recreates the affected client and clears old buffers.
rotation_restore.master_key_rotation: Initial recommended scope is offline/maintenance only. Stop all NVR/database writers and backup jobs; provision fresh active plus old decrypt-only key; administrative utility verifies every old envelope, reserves new-key attempts, re-encrypts all bounded rows atomically and verifies output. Restart using new active key; retain old key separately for old backups until their operator-approved retirement. No automatic key deletion.
rotation_restore.rotation_failure: Missing old key, bad tag, changed row, accounting/entropy failure or disk-full aborts row conversion; original ciphertext remains usable with old key. New-key attempt reservations remain burned. Keep both key slots and do not retire old key until verification succeeds.
rotation_restore.restore_encrypted_backup: Keep restored instance offline; obtain required backup decryption key from separate escrow and a fresh active write key, verify integrity/envelopes, re-encrypt all credentials before enabling writes/delivery. Missing key means blocked credentials, not reset or guessed password.
rotation_restore.restore_plaintext_backup: Use new binary/structural upgrade and explicit data migration before destination delivery or new backups. Keep old backup protected; do not label its bytes encrypted merely because current rows migrate.
rotation_restore.rollback: Within failed migration/rotation transaction preserve old representation. Binary/schema downgrade is unsupported and must fail explicitly; recovery from separately protected snapshots is a separate forward-migration procedure.
rotation_restore.key_retention: No invented expiry. Old decryption keys persist in separately controlled escrow exactly as long as approved retained encrypted backups require; D3 defines custody/retirement/recovery verification.

deployment_compatibility.observed: Dockerfile runs UID:GID10001:10001; Compose has separate config/database volumes; entrypoint preserves operator file permissions.
deployment_compatibility.proposal: Dedicated read-only keyring mount outside those volumes, readable only by UID10001; no auto-chown/chmod or auto-key generation.
deployment_compatibility.qualification: Not implemented or tested on released images/platforms.

deployment_compatibility.observed: scripts/install.sh generates a root-run systemd unit and 0755 data paths.
deployment_compatibility.proposal: Use the same file provider with root-owned0400 keyring outside data/backups; document exact service environment/drop-in provisioning without treating existing0755 directories as adequate secret storage.
deployment_compatibility.qualification: Requires owner deployment decision and disposable service tests; no physical/MIPS qualification.

deployment_compatibility.observed: T5 leaves named constrained device/toolchain and physical measurements deferred. Existing LPR uses getrandom/mbedTLS but that does not prove this feature works on every old kernel/build.
deployment_compatibility.proposal: Fail closed if required entropy/GCM/provider facilities unavailable; no plaintext or weak entropy fallback.
deployment_compatibility.qualification: Deferred, not silently removed from target inventory.

deployment_compatibility.observed: No supported provider contract established here; archive snippets are not deployment qualification.
deployment_compatibility.proposal: Operator may provision regular read-only file by an approved adapter; symlink projection/rotation semantics need separate compatibility tests.

unresolved_decisions.question: Accept the proposed degraded startup/backup-blocking policy when credentials cannot be migrated/decrypted, versus fail whole service startup?
unresolved_decisions.recommendation: Keep recording available, block credential-dependent delivery and new plaintext backups, expose explicit failure.

unresolved_decisions.question: Choose actual provisioning/custody owner and secret-file delivery for each supported deployment.
unresolved_decisions.recommendation: Dedicated operator-managed read-only regular file outside config/DB backups; no auto-generated app key or LPR-key reuse.

unresolved_decisions.question: Approve offline master-key rotation window, key escrow and backup retention/restore responsibilities.
unresolved_decisions.recommendation: Bounded offline atomic rotation with old-key escrow; no silent retirement or arbitrary expiry.

unresolved_decisions.question: Qualify old-kernel/embedded entropy and projected-secret/service permissions.
unresolved_decisions.recommendation: Retain unqualified targets explicitly until real platform evidence exists.

unresolved_decisions.question: Inventory historical plaintext copies and decide broker-password rotation/retirement procedure.
unresolved_decisions.recommendation: Treat historical copies as still exposed; revoke old broker credentials through separately authorized operations where needed.

validation_matrix.expected: No nonempty legacy bytes; authenticated create/read/update succeeds; redacted API/audit; private file/backup checks.

validation_matrix.case: Missing, unreadable, symlinked, wrong-owner, broad-mode, oversized or malformed keyring
validation_matrix.expected: No replacement/default key; metadata/recording policy follows D1; secret writes/delivery fail closed without mutation.

validation_matrix.case: Bad ciphertext, nonce, tag, key ID, UUID/AAD or length
validation_matrix.expected: No plaintext output; zeroed caller buffer; explicit nonsensitive failure; no anonymous retry.

validation_matrix.case: RNG short read/EINTR/error, duplicate nonce, count exhaustion, failed/stale write
validation_matrix.expected: Correct bounded entropy handling; reject a nonce matching a current envelope and entropy failures; never deliberately reuse a nonce; counts consumed even if data transaction fails. Historical random collisions are not exhaustively tracked.

validation_matrix.case: Existing API omit/clear/replace and stale revision
validation_matrix.expected: Preserved semantics and generation/reconnect behavior; malformed operations do not mutate prior credential.

validation_matrix.case: Legacy upgrade at0,1,64rows; failure at each transaction boundary
validation_matrix.expected: All-or-none data conversion; original associations/revisions preserved; missing key blocks legacy delivery; subsequent retry deterministic in state, fresh in nonces.

validation_matrix.case: Master-key rotation and crash/disk-full/missing old key
validation_matrix.expected: Atomic new representation or retained old representation; no early old-key retirement; explicit restart requirement.
Fresh write key required; old key decrypt-only; no old-counter write reuse; wrong/missing key leaves credentials blocked.
Old password-column SQL errors and explicit down refusal; never regenerate plaintext or silently authenticate anonymously.

validation_matrix.case: DB/WAL/journal/backup raw marker scan after migration
validation_matrix.expected: New writes contain no supplied plaintext marker; historical artifacts separately reported/retired, no whole-device erasure claim.

validation_matrix.case: Real MQTT reconnect and secret replacement
validation_matrix.expected: Authenticate with valid recovered credential, reject wrong key without connection fallback, preserve pending delivery semantics and clear superseded runtime buffers.

sources.verified_claim: GCM supports256-bit keys; use crypt_and_tag only for encryption and auth_decrypt to verify decryption tags. No claim that local builds are certified.
Sections8.2.2/8.3 require at least96random IV bits and a global2^32 invocation limit for the random construction; IV uniqueness is critical. This design still requires implementation/entropy review.
Logical deletion need not remove old content; secure_delete has documented limits. It is not a statement about external snapshots or device erasure.
VACUUM rewrites a database and has locking/free-space requirements; not an in-transaction or universal physical-erasure promise.
Readers can depend on WAL content and delay checkpoint progress; do not manually discard a live WAL.
